    Coordinate readers and writers of the output directory during its two installation moves.
    Post-commit backup, staging and progress observer failures are warnings on the successful result.

    <param name="request">
    The exact profile, destination, and activated runtime compilation generation.

    </param>
    <param name="cancellationToken">
    The token that cancels work before directory installation begins.
    </param>
    <returns>
    The durable output identity and deployment metrics.
    </returns>
    <exception cref="T:System.OperationCanceledException">
    Thrown when cancellation is requested before commit.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.DirectoryNotFoundException">
    The target Support Pack is missing; prepare it before starting the owner-thread build snapshot.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.InvalidDataException">
    The target Support Pack is present but invalid.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.IOException">
    Output installation fails before a complete candidate is committed.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.AggregateException">
    Output installation and restoration both fail; the previous tree remains at the reported backup path.
    </exception>
</member>

    <summary>
    Acquires reading ownership and verifies the complete artifact before exposing it to a consumer.
    </summary>
    <param name="ownerDirectory">
    The exact publisher root retaining the persistent owner.lock gate.
    </param>
    <param name="directory">
    The absolute artifact directory owned by its publisher; its persistent lease is stored alongside it.
    </param>
    <param name="fingerprint">
    The exact input identity required by the consumer.
    </param>
    <param name="outputDirectories">
    The complete relative output roots declared by the publisher.
    </param>
    <param name="cancellationToken">
    Cancels ownership acquisition without releasing another reader's protection.
    </param>
    <param name="statistics">
    Optional borrowed operation receiving output-integrity read statistics; its input cache is not used.
    </param>
    <returns>
    Reading ownership which the caller must retain until all artifact access completes.
    </returns>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentException">
    The directory is not absolute or a required identity is blank.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.InvalidDataException">
    The complete artifact does not match the requested identity and output inventory.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.TimeoutException">
    Repair or retirement retains exclusive ownership for more than thirty seconds.

    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.ObjectDisposedException">

    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">

<member name="M:Inno.Editor.Core.EditorModule.Stop(Inno.Editor.Core.EditorContext)">
    <summary>
    Stops the module before the containing extension generation is released.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Also compensates a partially failed Start. Completed stops are idempotent; pending stops may be retried.
    </remarks>
    <param name="context">
    The shared editor context for the runtime being stopped.
    </param>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentNullException">
    Thrown when <paramref name="context"/> is <see langword="null"/>.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.ObjectDisposedException">
    Thrown after the module has been disposed.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:Inno.Core.Execution.RetirementPendingException">
    Live work still depends on this module. Its owner must retain it and retry Stop before disposal.
    </exception>
</member>

    and preserve unfinished ownership; completed steps must be idempotent across retries.
    </remarks>

    <param name="preservedRows">

    <summary>
    Runs a frozen game deployment using explicitly supplied host services.
    </summary>
    <param name="options">
    The prepared content and platform service composition.
    </param>
    <param name="cancellationToken">
    Requests termination of frame scheduling.
    </param>
    <returns>
    Zero after orderly shutdown; startup, execution and retirement failures propagate.

    their synchronization context. A blocking host can use OwnerThreadExecution.Run.

    Options or a required host service is null.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.OperationCanceledException">

    <exception cref="T:System.IO.InvalidDataException">

    in an isolated catalog for validation without publishing Changed; ordinary mutations and generation changes are deferred.
    Rollback must finish before the pipeline or any validation dependency can be released.
    </remarks>

    Starts background indexing after cloning, then adopts its completed catalog without waiting.
    </summary>

    True when the candidate is indexed and ready for BeginValidation; false while preparation is pending.
    </returns>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">

</member>

    </param>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentNullException">

    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    The candidate is not indexed, validation already started, or the transaction is finished.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Assets.Pipeline.AssetSampleImportTransaction.Commit(System.Action{Inno.Assets.AssetPath})">
    <summary>
    Publishes a successfully validated import exactly once, without waiting for unfinished work.
    </summary>
    <param name="beforePublish">
    Optional owner-thread finalization, such as recording neutral History data. Failure leaves the
    transaction open for Rollback and no Changed notification is published.
    </param>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    Validation is unfinished, the transaction is finished, or the caller is not its owner thread.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.OperationCanceledException">
    The import or its validation was canceled before publication.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Assets.Pipeline.AssetSampleImportTransaction.Cancel">
    <summary>
    Requests cancellation of copying and validation while retaining all dependencies.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Cancellation does not wait. Continue owner-thread retirement until Rollback or Dispose completes.
    </remarks>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Assets.Pipeline.AssetSampleImportTransaction.Rollback">

    Cancels work and removes an uncommitted copy after all background consumers have drained.
    </summary>

    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Assets.Pipeline.AssetSampleImportTransaction.Dispose">

</member>

<member name="T:Inno.Assets.AssetDatabase">
    <summary>
    Loads canonical runtime assets exclusively from a verified catalog and content-addressed artifact bundles.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    This database never reads project source files, creates source mounts, runs importers, or writes content.
    One runtime session owns one database instance and disposes it before releasing its identity services.
    </remarks>
    <summary>
    Separates immutable artifact preparation from owner-thread asset materialization.
    </summary>
</member>

    <summary>
    Creates a read-only runtime asset database from one verified immutable content store.
    </summary>
    <param name="content">
    The borrowed content store; its owner closes it after this database and all outstanding reads retire.
    </param>
    <param name="serialization">
    The immutable converter generation pinned by the owning runtime session.
    </param>
    <param name="identities">
    The session-owned allocator used for canonical runtime asset identities.
    </param>
    <param name="types">
    The immutable type generation pinned by this runtime session, without refreshing authoring registries.
    </param>
    <param name="residencyBudgetBytes">
    Maximum unpinned runtime payload bytes retained after lease release.
    </param>
    <param name="preparationBudgetBytes">
    Maximum encoded payload bytes reserved by unfinished cold-load closures, independently of residency.
    </param>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentNullException">
    Thrown when <paramref name="serialization"/> is null.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.InvalidDataException">
    Thrown when the deployed catalog or its runtime artifact closure is incomplete or malformed.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Assets.AssetLease`1.Dispose">
    <summary>
    Releases this caller's residency ownership, retaining its value and callback while the provider reports Pending.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Pending may be wrapped in another exception; classify the complete failure with RetirementPendingException.Find.
    Ordinary sibling failures remain observable after a later release attempt succeeds.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:Inno.Core.Execution.RetirementPendingException">
    Provider retirement is unfinished or a concurrent release is in progress; retain this lease and retry at a safe point.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.AggregateException">
    The provider reports a wrapped failure, or release completes with ordinary errors retained from earlier pending attempts.
    </exception>
</member>

    <summary>
    Releases artifact ownership, retaining metadata and callback while the provider reports Pending.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Pending may be wrapped in another exception; classify the complete failure with RetirementPendingException.Find.
    Ordinary sibling failures remain observable after a later release attempt succeeds.
    New reads stop when release begins; already opened streams retain their independent provider pins.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:Inno.Core.Execution.RetirementPendingException">

</member>

    <summary>
    Recreates one component without invoking Reset and restores its persistent properties.
    </summary>
    <param name="owner">
    The live GameObject that will own the component.
    </param>
    <param name="type">
    The reload-safe identity of the current component implementation.

    <param name="persistentId">
    The component instance identity to preserve.
    </param>
    <param name="componentIndex">
    The requested attachment index.
    </param>
    <param name="stateData">
    Complete neutral element bytes produced by CaptureState, including missing-state metadata.
    </param>
    <param name="serialization">
    The serialization registry that owns the active converter generation.
    </param>
    <param name="assets">
    The resolver used to materialize canonical asset references in restored properties.
    </param>
    <returns>
    The recreated component, or a preserved missing placeholder when its logical type is unavailable.
    </returns>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentNullException">
    Thrown when <paramref name="owner"/> is <see langword="null"/>.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.InvalidDataException">
    Thrown when the payload is invalid or the stable type resolves to an incompatible component.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    Thrown when the identity or component multiplicity conflicts, property restoration is incomplete,
    or a failed restoration cannot remove its partially created component.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="T:Inno.Scene.ScenePropertySerialization">
    <summary>
    Captures and restores individual scene-object properties while preserving scene reference identities.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Each operation borrows its owning Core identity domain and resolves current references within that scene.
    Property access does not enumerate unrelated scene objects. Complete graph and prefab operations keep
    their explicit frozen local-identity boundaries. Asset references retain the supplied resolver context.
    </remarks>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Execution.LifetimeScope.Cancel">
    <summary>
    Stops new registrations and invokes cancellation callbacks on the calling thread.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Callbacks must return promptly. Dependent resources remain owned while cancellation callbacks execute,
    including when another thread attempts disposal. A callback reporting pending work permanently blocks release.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:System.AggregateException">
    One or more cancellation callbacks fail.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Execution.LifetimeScope.Dispose">
    <summary>
    Releases a quiescent lifetime in reverse registration order, continuing after ordinary cleanup failures.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Pending retirement retains the current resource and all remaining dependencies for a later attempt.
    Concurrent or reentrant retirement reports pending work without invoking a resource twice.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    Tracked work remains active; drain it before retrying.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.AggregateException">
    Cancellation, work or resource retirement fails.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Execution.LifetimeScope.DisposeAsync">
    <summary>
    Cancels and asynchronously drains tracked work before reverse-order release.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Only use asynchronous disposal for thread-neutral resources. Control-thread owners must await their work
    and call synchronous disposal at their own safe point; this method does not marshal to an owner thread.
    </remarks>
    <returns>
    A task that completes only after work and resource retirement finish.
    </returns>
    <exception cref="T:System.AggregateException">
    Cancellation, work or resource retirement fails.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="T:Inno.Core.Execution.OwnerThreadExecution">

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Execution.OwnerThreadExecution.Run``1(System.Func{System.Threading.Tasks.Task{``0}})">
    <summary>
    Pumps continuations until the owned operation completes, then restores the previous context.
    </summary>
    <typeparam name="TResult">
    The result produced by the operation.
    </typeparam>
    <param name="operation">
    Work that owns and retires every task it starts before returning. Async void work is not supported.
    </param>
    <returns>
    The completed operation result. Operation failures and cancellation propagate unchanged.
    </returns>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentNullException">
    The operation is null.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    The operation returned a null task.
    </exception>
    <remarks>
    This is a blocking host boundary. Callback-driven hosts use their platform synchronization
    context instead. Work that explicitly suppresses context capture is responsible for returning
    to the owner before accessing thread-affine resources.
    </remarks>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Execution.RetirementBarrier.TryComplete(System.Action)">
    <summary>
    Attempts retirement once at an owner-thread safe point.
    </summary>
    <param name="retire">
    The owner's retryable retirement operation; the barrier never retains this delegate.
    </param>
    <returns>
    True after retirement completes, or false while work remains within its deadline.
    </returns>
    <remarks>
    Wrapped pending failures retain their ownership semantics. A nested timeout is rethrown in its original
    exception tree. Ordinary sibling failures survive retries and are reported once retirement completes.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:System.AggregateException">
    Retirement completed after earlier ordinary failures, or the owner reported a wrapped terminal timeout.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:Inno.Core.Execution.RetirementTimeoutException">
    Work exceeded its deadline. The barrier remains terminally faulted and dependencies must be retained.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    The caller is not the thread that created this barrier.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.IO.AtomicDirectory.Publish(System.String,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)">
    <summary>
    Publishes a complete directory at an unoccupied path without replacing an existing destination.
    </summary>
    <param name="source">
    The complete candidate directory, disjoint from the destination.
    </param>
    <param name="destination">
    The unoccupied publication path on the same filesystem.
    </param>
    <param name="cancellationToken">
    Cancels preparation or bounded waits before the rename commits.
    </param>
    <remarks>
    Windows access and sharing failures are retried for at most two seconds to tolerate temporary readers.
    Failure preserves the candidate and any existing destination. A committed rename is not canceled afterward.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentException">
    A path is blank or the two directory trees overlap.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.DirectoryNotFoundException">
    The source directory does not exist.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.IOException">
    The destination exists, the filesystem cannot rename the tree, or a transient block persists.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.UnauthorizedAccessException">
    The operating system continues denying access after the bounded retry window.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.OperationCanceledException">
    Cancellation is requested before the directory is published.
    </exception>
</member>

symbols.documentation:
<member name="M:Inno.Core.IO.AtomicDirectory.Install(System.String,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)">
    <summary>
    Installs a disjoint candidate tree and restores the previous destination if installation fails.
    </summary>
    <param name="source">
    The complete candidate directory.
    </param>
    <param name="destination">
    The destination directory.
    </param>
    <param name="cancellationToken">
    Cancels preparation or bounded rename waits before the candidate commits.
    </param>
    <remarks>
    The caller must serialize readers and writers while the two directory moves run.
    Cancellation before commit restores the previous destination without canceling rollback.
    A committed candidate is not canceled afterward.
    Backup cleanup runs after commit; its failure preserves the installed candidate and remaining backup.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentException">
    Either path is blank, or the candidate and destination trees overlap.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.DirectoryNotFoundException">
    The candidate directory does not exist.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.IOException">
    Installation fails before the candidate becomes authoritative.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:Inno.Core.IO.DirectoryCleanupException">
    Installation committed, but the old backup could not be removed. The installed tree remains complete.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.UnauthorizedAccessException">
    The operating system denies access before the candidate can be installed.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.AggregateException">
    Installation and restoration both fail; neither tree is deleted to force a rollback.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.OperationCanceledException">
    Cancellation is requested before the candidate commits; any moved previous tree is restored.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.IO.AtomicFile.Install(System.String,System.String,System.Boolean)">
    <summary>
    Atomically installs an existing same-directory candidate file.
    </summary>
    <param name="source">
    The complete candidate file beside the destination.
    </param>
    <param name="destination">
    The destination file path beside the candidate.
    </param>
    <param name="overwrite">
    Whether an existing destination may be replaced; false never overwrites an external creator.
    </param>
    <remarks>
    A failed create-only publication preserves the candidate. After successful publication the
    candidate is removed; a subsequent cleanup failure reports that the complete target exists.
    Unix create-only publication requires same-directory hard-link support. The caller must own
    the candidate and parent directory until the operation completes.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.IOException">
    Publication fails, create-only mode finds an existing destination, or candidate retirement
    fails after the complete destination has been published.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.PlatformNotSupportedException">
    The host does not provide an atomic create-only filesystem primitive.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.IO.FileLease.AcquireAsync(System.String,System.TimeSpan,System.Threading.CancellationToken)">
    <summary>
    Waits for exclusive ownership without blocking an owner thread or changing shared data.
    </summary>
    <param name="path">
    The absolute lease file path; all participants must use the same persistent path.
    </param>
    <param name="timeout">
    The maximum wait, or <see cref="F:System.Threading.Timeout.InfiniteTimeSpan"/> for no time limit.
    </param>
    <param name="cancellationToken">
    Cancels waiting before ownership is returned.
    </param>
    <returns>
    The exclusive lease whose disposal permits the next participant to acquire ownership.
    </returns>
    <remarks>
    Lease files remain after disposal. Removing them would let Unix processes lock different
    inodes for the same path while an earlier participant still owns the original inode.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentException">
    The path is empty or relative, or the timeout is negative and not infinite.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.TimeoutException">
    Another participant retains ownership beyond the permitted wait.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.OperationCanceledException">
    Waiting was canceled; no lease is returned.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.IOException">
    The lease cannot be opened for a reason other than competing ownership.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.UnauthorizedAccessException">
    The operating system denies access to the lease path.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="T:Inno.Core.IO.PathBoundary">
    <summary>
    Resolves paths while enforcing an explicit filesystem ownership boundary.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Ownership uses ordinal spelling on every filesystem, including case-insensitive volumes.
    Callers must retain the root's spelling when constructing child paths. Case aliases are
    deliberately rejected: operating-system identity does not determine volume case semantics.
    </remarks>
</member>

    <summary>

    </summary>
    <param name="root">
    The trusted ownership root, which may not exist yet.
    </param>
    <param name="path">
    The absolute existing or future path beneath that root.
    </param>

    The path escapes the boundary or an existing entry is a link or reparse point.
    </exception>

    it does not grant protection against unrelated actors replacing paths after validation.
    </remarks>
</member>

    <summary>
    Creates a directory protected by this process lifetime when the caller can retain only file metadata.
    Payload consumers in other processes must register their lifetimes before using it.
    </summary>
    <param name="root">
    The absolute producer root; existing directories are never adopted.
    </param>
    <param name="identity">
    A current operation's explicit 32-digit hexadecimal directory identity shared by its process participants.
    </param>
    <param name="cancellationToken">
    Cancels before the process claim is transferred.
    </param>
    <returns>
    The new directory, preserved until every recorded process exits and the producer retires it.
    No managed lease object is retained by the caller.
    </returns>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.IOException">
    Ownership cannot be established within the boundary.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentException">
    The producer root or current operation identity is invalid.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.InvalidDataException">
    An existing operation claim is malformed, inactive, or cannot authorize this process.
    </exception>
</member>

    Owns the persistent-to-runtime identity map for one isolated runtime session.
    </summary>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityAllocator.#ctor">
    <summary>
    Creates an isolated runtime identity domain.
    </summary>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    Thrown if the process exhausts the available identity-domain values.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="P:Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityAllocator.hasCurrent">
    <summary>
    Gets whether the current asynchronous execution context is bound to an allocator.
    </summary>
</member>

<member name="P:Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityAllocator.current">
    <summary>
    Gets the allocator bound to the current asynchronous execution context.
    </summary>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    Thrown when the caller is outside a runtime session execution scope.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="P:Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityAllocator.count">
    <summary>
    Gets the number of currently registered identity entries.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Registry entries are weak. An entry whose object has been collected may remain counted until a lookup
    or registration observes and removes it. This property is not a strong-reference count or a liveness test.
    </remarks>
</member>

<member name="P:Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityAllocator.domainId">
    <summary>
    Gets the process-unique domain that qualifies every runtime identity allocated here.
    </summary>
</member>

<member name="E:Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityAllocator.ObjectUnregistered">
    <summary>
    Occurs after an object has been permanently removed from this allocator.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Every observer is invoked. Multiple observer failures are reported as one
    <see cref="T:System.AggregateException"/> after notification completes.
    </remarks>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityAllocator.EnterScope">
    <summary>
    Binds this allocator to the current asynchronous execution context until the returned scope is disposed.
    </summary>
    <returns>
    A strict last-in-first-out scope owned by the caller.
    </returns>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    Thrown when scopes are disposed out of order.
    </exception>
</member>

symbols.signature: public bool Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityAllocator.Register(Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityObject obj, System.Guid? persistentId = null)
symbols.documentation:
<member name="M:Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityAllocator.Register(Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityObject,System.Nullable{System.Guid})">
    <summary>
    Registers an object and assigns its session-local runtime identity.
    </summary>
    <param name="obj">
    The identity object owned by this runtime session.
    </param>
    <param name="persistentId">
    An optional persistent identity override. When omitted, the object's existing persistent identity is retained.
    An empty resolved identity is replaced with a newly generated identity.
    </param>
    <returns>
    <see langword="true"/> when the object was newly registered; otherwise, <see langword="false"/>.
    </returns>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentNullException">
    Thrown when <paramref name="obj"/> is null.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    Thrown when a different live object is already registered with the resolved persistent identity.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityAllocator.InitializePersistentIdentity(Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityObject,System.Guid)">
    <summary>
    Assigns a persistent identity to a detached object without allocating a runtime identity.
    </summary>
    <param name="obj">
    The detached identity object to initialize.
    </param>
    <param name="persistentId">
    The non-empty persistent identity to assign.
    </param>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentNullException">
    Thrown when <paramref name="obj"/> is null.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentException">
    Thrown when <paramref name="persistentId"/> is empty.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    Thrown when the object already has a live runtime identity.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityAllocator.Unregister(Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityObject)">
    <summary>
    Removes an object from this session and notifies every unregistration observer.
    </summary>
    <param name="obj">
    The identity object to remove.
    </param>
    <returns>
    <see langword="true"/> when the object was registered; otherwise, <see langword="false"/>.
    </returns>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentNullException">
    Thrown when <paramref name="obj"/> is null.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.AggregateException">
    Thrown after removal when one or more observers fail.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="T:Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityDomainId">
    <summary>
    Identifies one isolated runtime identity namespace within the current process.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Domain identifiers are runtime-only values. They must never be serialized or used as persistent object identity.
    </remarks>
</member>

    </summary>
</member>

    </summary>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityDomainId.Equals(Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityDomainId)">

    The domain identifier to compare with this value.
    </param>
    <returns>
    <see langword="true"/> when both values identify the same domain; otherwise, <see langword="false"/>.

</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Identity.IdentityDomainId.Equals(System.Object)">

</member>

<member name="T:Inno.Core.Identity.RuntimeIdentity">

    Addresses a live identity object within one explicitly identified runtime domain.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    This value is suitable for transient interaction payloads only and must never be persisted.
    Equality compares the stored domain and runtime identifier; it does not verify that an object is still live.
    </remarks>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Logging.FileLogSink.Receive(Inno.Core.Logging.LogEntry)">
    <summary>
    Writes and flushes one complete entry before returning, serializing concurrent callers.
    </summary>
    <param name="entry">
    The immutable entry to persist.
    </param>
    <remarks>
    The router owns scheduling and backpressure. Write failures propagate to its sink quarantine.
    Retention cannot remove files locked by another active writer and retries them on later rotation.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:System.ObjectDisposedException">
    The sink has been disposed.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.IOException">
    An entry cannot be written, flushed or rotated.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.UnauthorizedAccessException">
    The caller cannot create the next log file or access the directory.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    A previous failed rotation left no writable file.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Logging.FileLogSink.Dispose">

symbols.documentation: Linearly interpolates between two values. This method is a less efficient, more precise version of . See remarks for more info. Source value. Destination value. Value between 0 and 1 indicating the weight of value2. Interpolated value. This method performs the linear interpolation based on the following formula: ((1 - amount) * value1) + (value2 * amount). Passing amount a value of 0 will cause value1 to be returned, a value of 1 will cause value2 to be returned. This method does not have the floating point precision issue that has. i.e. If there is a big gap between value1 and value2 in magnitude (e.g. value1=10000000000000000, value2=1), right at the edge of the interpolation range (amount=1), will return 0 (whereas it should return 1). This also holds for value1=10^17, value2=10; value1=10^18,value2=10^2... so on. For an in depth explanation of the issue, see below references: Relevant Wikipedia Article: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_interpolation#Programming_language_support Relevant StackOverflow Answer: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/4353525/floating-point-linear-interpolation#answer-23716956

Represents a mutable four-by-four transformation matrix using column-vector multiplication. Conventions used by this type: Column-vector math: points/vectors are treated as column vectors on the right: v' = M * v. Translation is stored in the last column: (m14, m24, m34). Matrix multiplication follows standard form: C = A * B (apply B then A in column-vector convention: A * (B * v)). Note on handedness: This type is handedness-agnostic. Handedness is determined by the specific factory (e.g. and are currently left-handed). If your engine convention is right-handed (-Z forward), add/use explicit RH variants (e.g. CreateLookAtRH / CreatePerspectiveFieldOfViewRH).

    <summary>
    Requests a compile-time serialization converter for a closed data-transfer type.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    The annotated type must implement <see cref="T:Inno.Core.Serialization.ISerializable"/>, expose a constructor that generated
    code can invoke, and use <see cref="T:Inno.Core.Serialization.SerializablePropertyAttribute"/> on every persisted member.
    Types with polymorphic identity, reference graphs, or custom restoration invariants must use an
    explicit converter instead.
    </remarks>

<member name="M:Inno.Core.Serialization.SerializationRegistry.CaptureSnapshot``1(``0,Inno.Core.Serialization.SerializationContext,Inno.Core.Serialization.SerializationSnapshot)">
    <summary>
    Captures complete serialized state while sharing unchanged neutral values with a previous capture.
    </summary>
    <typeparam name="T">
    The exact concrete root type, interpreted by the current converter generation.
    </typeparam>
    <param name="value">
    The non-null root captured through its current converter and declared complete inputs.
    </param>
    <param name="context">
    The complete owner context, including required reference resolvers.
    </param>
    <param name="previous">
    An optional immutable capture to reuse; it is never changed or retained by this registry.
    </param>
    <returns>
    The previous instance when all captured values can be reused, otherwise a new immutable snapshot.
    Reference equality proves unchanged bytes; different instances may still encode identically.
    Ordinary serialization and snapshot encoding produce identical bytes. Capture failure publishes no snapshot.
    </returns>
    <remarks>
    Writers borrowed by a snapshot converter belong to its synchronous callback and must not be used after it returns.
    Default capture evaluates getters and converters in full. An explicitly opted-in converter may
    reuse its prior node only after every current capture-key input has been verified. Ordinary
    serialization never uses these keys; incomplete or unavailable declarations retain complete capture.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentNullException">
    The source value is null.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.ObjectDisposedException">
    The registry has been disposed.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    A converter, unsupported value or reference context prevents capture.
    </exception>
</member>

    <summary>
    Accepts explicit declarations and linked generic factories while a static catalog is being composed.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Generated contributors run synchronously on the composition thread and must not retain the registrar.
    Its registrations belong to the resulting generation. Constructors execute only when requested.
    </remarks>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Extensibility.Catalogs.ITypeCatalogRegistrar.Register(Inno.Extensibility.Catalogs.TypeCatalogMetadata,System.Func{System.Object})">
    <summary>
    Registers immutable discovery metadata and an optional parameterless construction function.
    </summary>
    <param name="metadata">
    Complete discovery facts for one assembly-local declaration.
    </param>
    <param name="factory">
    Creates a new instance, or null when the declaration is not constructible.
    </param>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentException">
    The declaration has already been registered.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    The caller runs on another thread or retained this registrar after catalog composition completed.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Extensibility.Catalogs.ITypeCatalogRegistrar.RegisterFactory(System.Type,System.Func{System.Object})">
    <summary>
    Registers a closed generic construction linked by the contributing assembly.
    </summary>
    <param name="type">
    A fully closed generic type whose definition is contributed by the completed catalog.
    </param>
    <param name="factory">
    Creates a new instance of the linked construction without dynamic code generation.
    </param>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentException">
    The type is not a fully closed generic construction.
    </exception>
    <remarks>
    Repeated registrations of the same closed construction are idempotent; the first factory is retained.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    The caller runs on another thread or retained this registrar after catalog composition completed.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Extensibility.Catalogs.ITypeCatalogRegistrar.RejectGenericConstruction(System.Type,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.Type})">
    <summary>
    Records a construction whose argument set was rejected by the declaration's compile-time constraints.
    </summary>
    <param name="definition">
    The generic declaration contributed by the completed catalog.
    </param>
    <param name="arguments">
    The complete closed argument set. The registrar copies this collection during registration.
    </param>
    <remarks>
    This fact lets static resolution skip an inapplicable converter without attempting dynamic generic creation.
    Unknown constructions remain explicit deployment errors. Repeated rejections are idempotent.
    </remarks>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentException">
    The declaration or argument set is incomplete, open, or conflicts with a registered factory.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentNullException">
    The declaration or argument collection is null.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.InvalidOperationException">
    The caller runs on another thread or retained this registrar after catalog composition completed.
    </exception>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Extensibility.Reload.GenerationCoordinator.EnsureRetirementSafe">

<member name="M:Inno.Scripting.Compiler.ScriptCompiler.CompileAuthoringGenerationAsync(System.IProgress{Inno.Scripting.Compiler.ScriptCompilationProgress},System.Threading.CancellationToken,Inno.Assets.Pipeline.IAssetSourceSnapshot)">
    <summary>
    Compiles a complete runtime and editor candidate generation without activating it.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Source discovery captures live inputs on the owner thread. Reference generation, Roslyn and
    artifact writes run in the background; progress observers must accept callbacks from either thread.
    Retain the source generation until the returned operation drains, including after cancellation.
    Complete cache trees use Core IO atomic publication and replacement. A committed cache remains
    valid if cleanup of its previous tree fails; compilation does not activate either generation.
    </remarks>
    <param name="progress">
    Optional observer for monotonic compiler progress.
    </param>
    <param name="cancellationToken">
    The token that cancels compilation before an artifact generation is committed.
    </param>
    <returns>
    The immutable diagnostics and artifacts produced by the compilation attempt.
    </returns>
    <exception cref="T:System.OperationCanceledException">
    Thrown when <paramref name="cancellationToken"/> is canceled.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.IOException">
    Artifact publication fails, or cleanup fails after a complete cache tree commits.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.UnauthorizedAccessException">
    The filesystem continues denying artifact access after the bounded Core IO wait.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.AggregateException">
    Cache replacement and restoration both fail; the exception identifies the preserved previous tree.
    </exception>
    <param name="sourceSnapshot">
    Optional isolated authoring sources. Capture on its owner thread and keep its transaction
    alive until compilation drains; null selects the current Plugin candidate or active sources.
    </param>
</member>

<member name="M:Inno.Scripting.Compiler.ScriptCompiler.CompileRuntimeDeploymentAsync(System.String,System.IProgress{Inno.Scripting.Compiler.ScriptCompilationProgress},System.Threading.CancellationToken)">
    <summary>
    Compiles only the runtime assembly closure required by a deployed Player and binds it to that Player runtime.
    </summary>
    <remarks>
    Complete cache trees use Core IO atomic publication and replacement. Cancellation before commit
    preserves the previous tree; cancellation does not undo a committed cache. Cleanup failure after
    commit preserves the installed tree and remaining backup without activating a generation.
    </remarks>
    <param name="targetRuntimeDirectory">
    The verified Player Support Pack directory whose runtime assemblies will execute the emitted scripts.
    </param>
    <param name="progress">
    Optional observer for monotonic compiler progress.
    </param>
    <param name="cancellationToken">
    The token that cancels compilation before an artifact generation is committed.
    </param>
    <returns>
    The immutable diagnostics and runtime-only artifacts produced by the compilation attempt.
    </returns>
    <exception cref="T:System.OperationCanceledException">
    Thrown when <paramref name="cancellationToken"/> is canceled.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentException">
    Thrown when <paramref name="targetRuntimeDirectory"/> is empty.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.DirectoryNotFoundException">
    Thrown when <paramref name="targetRuntimeDirectory"/> does not exist.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.InvalidDataException">
    Thrown when the target runtime has no valid Inno runtime assembly closure.
    </exception>
    <exception cref="T:System.IO.IOException">

    </exception>

    The complete surface is used when omitted.
    </param>
    <exception cref="T:System.ArgumentException">

    </param>

    <param name="primaryInputSurfaceSizeProvider">
